correctness.rationale: The principal ideal of x is indexed by gcd(x,p²q²), and containment reverses divisibility, so the cells are independent and joined exactly for incomparable divisors. Their sizes are phi(p²q²/d). Independently checked the seven-vertex quotient: B and D are the only degree-four vertices; between them are the direct edge and internally disjoint paths B–E–D, B–C–A–D, and B–F–G–D. The quotient has distinct open neighborhoods and no true-twin pair; the full graph's false-twin classes are precisely the cells. The quotient automorphisms independently reverse the endpoints (with path reversal) and exchange the length-three paths. B and D have different weights q(q−1) and p(p−1), so endpoints cannot swap in a weight-preserving action. The remaining path exchange would identify A with G, requiring q(p−1)=1. Thus only independent cell permutations remain. Each block requires all but one vertex to be fixed in a determining set and pairwise distinct colors to distinguish, and these conditions suffice, including singleton blocks. The sum of w−1 is N−7; the largest size is max(w_A,w_C), since these dominate the other sizes. The stated generator wording at line 70 is inaccurate (one involution cannot generate four elements); the list of three nonidentity elements and the weight argument are correct. The note about formally equal primes is not a theorem for Z/(p⁴). The packaged checker was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The calculation is for distinct primes; formally equal weights on a grid do not represent the divisor classes of a prime-power modulus.

originality.rationale: The full symmetry claim is already implied by Feng–Ma–Wang's cyclic power-graph automorphism theorem. In the additive cyclic group of Z/mZ, the subgroup generated by x is precisely Rx. Thus the complement of this cozero graph is the power graph with the universal vertices (0 and the units) removed. Example 5.1(ii), with its proof and Theorem 2.2, gives the actual full action as independent symmetric groups on the universal class and on every proper nontrivial order class for all non-prime-power m. Removing the universal class gives precisely the seven independent permutations at m=p²q². The two symmetry-breaking numbers follow mechanically from that same permutation action, not merely from an accidental equality of group orders. This is verified prior coverage, not a claim of falsity or a conclusion from an inaccessible source.
residual_risks: The unavailable 2022 full text may contain more overlap but is not needed for the verified implication. No claim of exhaustive literature coverage is made.

value.rationale: The proposed exact invariants for the balanced exponent slice are mechanical consequences of a known full cyclic-group power-graph action. Stating them in cozero terminology or giving an independent seven-vertex check does not address a remaining gap. The small unweighted quotient calculation describes why a weighted action can be rigid but, on its own, is an elementary path symmetry count with no separately motivated unresolved question in this record.
residual_risks: This does not preclude independent value for different cozero graphs not covered by cyclic power-graph results.
